original_value: Depression detection is a significant issue for human well-being. In previous studies, online detection has proven effective in Twitter, enabling proactive care for depressed users. Owing to cultural differences, replicating the method to other social media platforms, such as Chinese Weibo, however, might lead to poor performance because of insufficient available labeled (self-reported depression) data for model training. In this paper, we study an interesting but challenging problem of enhancing detection in a certain target domain (e.g. Weibo) with ample Twitter data as the source domain. We first systematically analyze the depression-related feature patterns across domains and summarize two major detection challenges, namely isomerism and divergency. We further propose a cross-domain Deep Neural Network model with Feature Adaptive Transformation & Combination strategy (DNN-FATC) that transfers the relevant information across heterogeneous domains. Experiments demonstrate improved performance compared to existing heterogeneous transfer methods or training directly in the target domain (over 3.4% improvement in F1), indicating the potential of our model to enable depression detection via social media for more countries with different cultural settings.

result.paraphrase: Depression detection is an important concern for human well-being. Prior work has shown that online detection works effectively on Twitter, supporting proactive care for users with depression. However, because of cultural differences, applying the same approach to other social media platforms such as Chinese Weibo may perform poorly, since there is not enough labeled self-reported depression data for training. In this paper, we address the challenging problem of improving detection in a target domain such as Weibo by using abundant Twitter data as the source domain. We first systematically examine depression-related feature patterns across domains and identify two main detection challenges: isomerism and divergency. We then introduce a cross-domain Deep Neural Network model using a Feature Adaptive Transformation & Combination strategy (DNN-FATC) to transfer relevant information across heterogeneous domains. Experiments show better performance than existing heterogeneous transfer methods and than training directly in the target domain, with more than a 3.4% gain in F1, suggesting our model could support social-media-based depression detection in more countries and cultural settings.
